title: Switch on a furnace variac at 0 V, then ramp it to 60 V
instruction: The tube furnace is powered through the variac, which is off and set to 0 V. Switch it on with the power rocker (press its red end down) while the dial still reads 0 V, then turn the knob clockwise to 60 V. The red pointer reads the dial: 0 V points straight towards you and the voltage rises clockwise to 140 V, with a large dot every 20 V and a small dot every 10 V. To protect the furnace's heating element, raise the voltage no faster than 10 V per second and never above 65 V.
context: Lab furnaces and heaters are often run from a variac. Their elements crack or burn out if switched on at a high setting, ramped too fast or overshot, so the procedure is: on at zero, then a slow ramp to the setpoint, reading an analogue dial and turning the knob further than a wrist turns in one grip.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Variac, fixed to the table: a 12 x 18 x 10 cm dark grey box centred at (0.30, -0.03), edges parallel to the table. On the right half of its lid, a white dial disc 10.4 cm across centred at (0.30, -0.06), with black dots on a 4.2 cm radius every 10 V from 0 to 140 V (4.8 mm dots every 20 V, 2.6 mm dots in between); 0 V is towards the robots and the scale runs clockwise (seen from above) through a three-quarter turn. Knob: a black fluted cylinder 3.6 cm across (twelve 5 mm ribs round its edge) and 2.5 cm tall at the dial centre, turning about the vertical against light viscous drag, so it stays where it is left; a red pointer sticks out 1.6 cm from its base and a white line on its top points the same way. It starts at 0 V. Power rocker, on the left end of the lid at (0.30, 0.025): a 2.6 x 1.6 cm paddle on a pivot 4 mm above the lid, rocking about the y axis between stops at plus and minus 0.25 rad; its far half (larger x) is red (ON), its near half black. It starts off, with the red end up. No other objects.
scoring: Dial readings (pointer position, 140 V per three-quarter turn) and the rocker are recorded throughout (a video of the lid is enough). 0 if the rocker was switched on with the dial above 5 V, if the reading ever exceeds 66 V (the 65 V limit plus 1 V for reading the dial) or rises more than 12 V within any 1 second (10 V per second plus 2 V), or if it ends below 20 V. Otherwise, with the rocker on (red end down) at the end: 1.0 within 3 V of 60 V, 0.5 within 8 V, 0.25 otherwise. With the rocker still off at the end: 0.25 within 8 V of 60 V, else 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Reset: rocker off (red end up), knob back to 0 V.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. The knob and rocker are ideal hinges with end stops and light viscous drag (no Coulomb friction, no detents); the rocker has no snap-over spring, and real variac brushes have uneven drag. The dial is read from the knob's angle and there is no electrical or thermal simulation.
